newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Chernomyrdin to discuss cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Chernomyrdin to discuss cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will on Thursday discuss a new cabinet line-up following Yeltsin's decision to reshuffle the government to make it more efficient and promote reforms, Interfax news agency reported.
The presidential press service said Yeltsin would meet the prime minister in the Kremlin at 1 p.m. (1000 GMT).
Yeltsin blasted the government for failing to tackle the economic and social crisis in Russia in his state of the nation address last Thursday and ordered Chernomyrdin to reorganise the cabinet.
He also made clear that Chernomyrdin and the newly-appointed First Deputy Prime Minister, Anatoly Chubais, would keep their posts in the new cabinet.
Chernomyrdin said on Wednesday the new cabinet, which he had promised to present later this week, would be younger and more professional and include market-minded reformers.
He added that most new ministers will be under 50 and have administrative experience.
Chubais would be the one and only first deputy premier -- there are four now -- while the number of deputy premiers and ministers would be cut.
Chubais is a hate figure for conservatives for his role in Russia's tough privatisation drive in 1992-1996 and spearheading of Yeltsin's re-election campaign last summer.
The communist-dominated State Duma lower house of parliament responded with an angry resolution condemning the nomination of Chubais but stopping short of attacking Yeltsin personally.
In a resolution approved by a thin majority, the chamber denounced the government policies as "ruinous" and branded Chubais' appointment as a "challenge" to the legislature.
The deputies made clear they wanted a role in the reshuffle, urging Yeltsin to hold consultations with parliament.
